title: Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For every forest $H$, and every $k$, every $H$-free graph that does not contain a clique on $k$ vertices has bounded chromatic number.
context_text: The Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture is the central motivation for this paper's line of research. It is known when $H$ is a path (Gyárfás [6], the original paper proposing the conjecture), but remains open for general forests. The present paper strengthens the path case by proving polynomial bounds under exclusion of complete $d$-partite graphs.
paper_contribution: Proves Theorem 1.5 (paths are multibounding): for every path $H$ and all $d \geq 1$ there is a polynomial $f$ such that every $H$-free graph with no $K_d(t)$ subgraph satisfies $\chi(G) \leq f(t)$. Taking $t=1$ recovers Gyárfás' path case of the conjecture; the result is strictly stronger and extends to brooms and disjoint unions of multibounding forests.
notes: Attributed via citations [6] (Gyárfás) and [20] (Sumner) in the paper's introduction.
paper_title: Polynomial bounds for chromatic number VIII. Excluding a path and a complete multipartite graph

title: Conjecture 1.6
context_text: $H$-free means having no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $K_d(t)$ denotes the complete $d$-partite graph with all parts of size $t$ (excluded here as a subgraph, not necessarily induced). A graph $H$ is multibounding if for every $d\ge1$ there is a polynomial $f(t)$ such that, for all $t\ge1$, every $H$-free graph $G$ with no $K_d(t)$ subgraph satisfies $\chi(G)\le f(t)$. Taking $t=1$ ($K_d(1)=K_d$) shows that every multibounding graph is a forest satisfying the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (for every forest $H$ and every $k$, $H$-free graphs with no $K_k$ have bounded chromatic number), so this conjecture strengthens Gyárfás–Sumner; conversely, every forest satisfying the polynomial version of Gyárfás–Sumner (chromatic number polynomial in the clique number for $H$-free graphs) is multibounding. For $d=2$ the statement is known for every forest: Rödl proved that $H$-free graphs with no $K_{t,t}$ subgraph have bounded chromatic number, and Scott, Seymour and Spirkl made the bound polynomial in $t$. Previously trees of radius two were known to be multibounding; the paper proves that paths and brooms (a path with leaves added at one end) are multibounding, and that a forest whose components are all multibounding is multibounding.
notes: Explicitly introduced with 'We propose: 1.6 Conjecture' in the paper.
